new_statements.quote: p.7: "Le ton a une fonction contrastive, servant à distinguer de nombreuses paires de mots autrement homonymes, et jouant aussi, en conjonction avec les pauses, un rôle syntaxique. Le rôle de l'accent d'intensité est expressif, et non contrastif." p.23: "L'accent d'intensité ne joue ni un rôle contrastif, comme en anglais, ni un rôle grammatical. Il a une fonction expressive n'ayant aucun rapport fixe avec l'intonation, et pouvant frapper tous les mots, quelle que soit leur classe. Il peut porter sur une monosyllabe; c'est généralement la deuxième syllabe des mots plus longs qui le porte, sauf dans le cas de pepe, qui peut être accentué sur les deux syllabes"
new_statements.translation: p.7: Tone has a contrastive function, distinguishing many otherwise homonymous word pairs and, together with pauses, playing a syntactic role. The role of the intensity accent is expressive, not contrastive. p.23: The intensity accent plays neither a contrastive role, as in English, nor a grammatical role. It has an expressive function with no fixed relation to intonation, and can strike any word whatever its class. It can fall on a monosyllable; in longer words it is generally the second syllable that carries it, except in the case of pepe, which can be accented on both syllables.
new_statements.citation: Samarin, William J. 1970. Sango, langue de l'Afrique centrale. Leiden: E. J. Brill. (statements on the VEHICULAR Sango, sang1328 [sag]; corroborated by Samarin 1963, A Grammar of Sango, p.1: 'Stress is not a significant feature of the phonemic structure of the language, but it is used expressively.')
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check. the p.7 passage is at lines 228-231 (printed p.7 = first page of 'CHAPITRE 1 LES PHONÈMES', par. 1) and reads exactly as quoted except an scanned artefact 'Le. ton' for 'Le ton'; the p.23 passage is at lines 738-744 ('3. L'accent d'intensité ne joue ni un rôle contrastif, comme en anglais, ni un rôle grammatical.. sauf dans le cas de pepe, qui peut être accentué sur les deux syllabes:'), followed by three examples and 'En outre, dans le cas de pepe, le ton est parfois altéré.', then the running head '24 L'INTONATION' and par. 4 on French-influenced speakers with 'un accent d'intensité, accompagné d'une baisse tonale, sur la dernière syllabe' (lines 758-765). Verbatim apart from…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Vehicular Sango (three tones H/M/L) has no phonological word stress; an expressive intensity accent, when used, normally lands on the second syllable of polysyllables (any word class), on the monosyllable itself in monosyllables. No corresponding statement for Riverain Sango proper was found; the accessible sister-lect descriptions (Yakoma: Boyeldieu 1975 excerpt; Ngbandi of Yakoma: Kamanda Kola 1989) describe only tone (3 levels + contours) and are silent on stress.
new_statements.exceptions: pepe (negator) may be accented on both syllables; French-influenced speakers add a final stressed vowel with high-falling glide, judged imitative of French with no contrastive or expressive function (1970 p.23-24 §4; 1963 p.29 §3.40).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement made within a chapter on intonation of the vehicular/creole Sango (sang1328), based on Samarin's 1950s-60s fieldwork in CAR; Samarin himself distinguishes it from 'vernacular Sango, one of the dialects of the Ngbandi complex' (= Riverain Sango). Samarin 1963's dedicated section 3.30 'Stress' (p.28) is on a page not filmed in the ERIC microfiche.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement (Samarin 1970/1963) describes the vehicular/creole Sango, Glottolog sang1328 [sag], NOT Riverain Sango rive1257 [snj]; Samarin himself separates 'vernacular Sango, one of the dialects of the Ngbandi complex' from creolized Sango, while noting the vehicular language keeps 'les traits fondamentaux du groupe ngbandi-yakoma-sango'. Riverain Sango is, per Boyeldieu (1975:16) and Boyeldieu & Diki-Kidiri (1982:16), one language with Ngbandi, Yakoma (yako1252), Dendi (dend1242) and Mbangi (mban1262); the Yakoma and Ngbandi-of-Yakoma descriptions opened here (Boyeldieu 1975 excerpt; Kamanda Kola 1989) are tonal (3 levels + contours) and silent on stress. Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for rive1257 (Bouquiaux et al. 1978 dictionary) is tagged to both sag and snj.

sources.note: VEHICULAR Sango [sag] sang1328, not Riverain Sango. p.7 (ch.1 §1): 'Le rôle de l'accent d'intensité est expressif, et non contrastif.' p.23 (ch.3 §3): intensity accent is neither contrastive nor grammatical, expressive only, may fall on a monosyllable, 'c'est généralement la deuxième syllabe des mots plus longs qui le porte, sauf dans le cas de pepe'. p.1: vehicular Sango keeps 'les traits fondamentaux du groupe ngbandi-yakoma-sango'. Three tones H/M/B (p.12).
